subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: For direct and normal group/channel conversations, should unphased assistant text before or between tool calls remain eligible for automatic visible delivery, or should visible output require final-answer/message-tool semantics by default?
rationale: The secure UX goal conflicts with shipped/default compatibility for users who rely on automatic bare-text replies, and current open PRs cover partial layers without deciding the permanent delivery contract.

options.title: Final-only source replies with compatibility escape
options.body: Make inter-tool/unphased assistant text private unless it is explicit final-answer text or a message-tool send, while preserving or documenting an operator-controlled automatic-final compatibility mode.

options.title: Default everything to message-tool-only
options.body: Require message(action=send) for user-visible source replies across direct, group, and channel conversations, accepting a higher upgrade break risk for existing bare-text workflows.

options.title: Land opt-in mitigations only
options.body: Keep current automatic defaults and ship opt-in guards such as enforceFinalTag or verbose-off suppression, accepting that unconfigured deployments may still leak intermediate text.

recommendation.title: Final-only source replies with compatibility escape
recommendation.body: Make inter-tool/unphased assistant text private unless it is explicit final-answer text or a message-tool send, while preserving or documenting an operator-controlled automatic-final compatibility mode.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for visible-reply policy and group/direct delivery defaults points to steipete's recent source-reply work.
